narrativeReportMd:
# CodeableConcept R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
No local hard instance-breaking changes were found for `CodeableConcept`. The R6 artifact exists under the same canonical URL and preserves the same local content model: optional/repeating `coding` of type `Coding` and optional `text` of type `string`.

## Scope
The report covers the CodeableConcept datatype definition itself. It excludes inherited `Element`/`DataType` members, global datatype hierarchy changes, nested `Coding` datatype changes, and profile/resource-specific bindings on CodeableConcept-valued elements.

## Main migration themes
For local CodeableConcept data, R4-to-R6 migration should not require adding, removing, renaming, or reshaping fields. Existing R4 fragments using `coding` and/or `text` remain structurally representable in R6. Tooling should still be aware that R6 metadata describes CodeableConcept as a `DataType` specialization and adds type-characteristic metadata used by binding/translation-aware tooling.

## Highest-impact findings
None for local CodeableConcept elements.

## Findings requiring human review
No local CodeableConcept findings require human review. Review is still useful for the separate `DataType` and `Coding` reports because those dependencies can affect generated models and nested validation behavior.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Because the local element model is unchanged, there is no local breaking design to justify or mitigate. The main compatibility concern is cross-artifact coordination: generated classes and validators must handle the R6 base datatype model and any separate `Coding` changes.

## Follow-up analysis
Assess `DataType` for the global base-definition/class-hierarchy change and `Coding` for nested coding conformance changes that can surface inside `CodeableConcept.coding`.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: No local hard or likely breaking CodeableConcept changes were found. The top migration concerns are outside this artifact: the R6 datatype base hierarchy, nested `Coding` changes, and profile-specific terminology bindings. The main uncertainty is the absence of an official diff or authored change note, though the computable definitions are clear.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Local CodeableConcept instances should round-trip at the `coding`/`text` container level without structural transformation. Migration programs should still test generated model inheritance, validators, and nested `Coding` behavior because those are dependencies used by CodeableConcept but not local CodeableConcept changes.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for the local content model because both primary StructureDefinitions and package index entries were available and the local differential/snapshot elements match for presence, cardinality, types, flags, and semantic text. Confidence would improve only modestly with official diff notes or authored narrative pages.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: The canonical URL, id, name, kind, type, derivation, status, and abstract flag are stable. The R6 `baseDefinition` shift to `DataType` is intentionally excluded as a base/datatype hierarchy dependency.
The local CodeableConcept differential still defines only the root, `coding`, and `text`. No local element was added, removed, renamed, moved, split, or merged.
`CodeableConcept.coding` remains type `Coding`; `CodeableConcept.text` remains type `string`. There are no local choice elements whose type domain changed.
No local CodeableConcept element is a `Reference`, so no reference target domain changed.

The CodeableConcept datatype itself has no local terminology binding on the root, `coding`, or `text`. Bindings applied by resource elements or profiles that use CodeableConcept are outside this artifact.

No local CodeableConcept-specific invariant was added, removed, or strengthened. The recurring `ele-1` constraint remains an inherited Element constraint; R6 omission of XPath metadata and generated condition placement are treated as base/tooling differences, not local findings.
No local fixed value, pattern value, or default value is present in either R4 or R6.
No local maxLength, regex, minValue, or maxValue constraint was found on CodeableConcept, `coding`, or `text`.
`isModifier` remains false for local CodeableConcept elements.
`coding` and `text` remain summary elements; no local summary flag change was found.
No local slicing is defined on `CodeableConcept.coding` or `CodeableConcept.text` in either version. The inherited `extension` slicing is outside local scope.

The local `short`, `definition`, `comment`, and `requirements` text for the root, `coding`, and `text` are materially unchanged. The package-level description was shortened only by removing the R4 prefix `Base StructureDefinition for`.
No local JSON/XML element names, cardinalities, or datatypes changed. Generated-code inheritance may change because R6 introduces `DataType` as the base, but that is a separate base-artifact concern.
At the CodeableConcept container level, R6 `coding` and `text` content is representable in R4. R6-only content inside nested `Coding` or inherited/base elements is outside this local assessment.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 adds CodeableConcept type-characteristic metadata
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R6 adds `structuredefinition-type-characteristics` values `can-bind` and `do-translations` at the StructureDefinition metadata level. These do not add required instance fields or change the JSON/XML representation of CodeableConcept.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Metadata-driven tooling should tolerate and, where useful, consume these R6 characteristics for binding and translation workflows. Tools that hard-code the R4 metadata extension set may need updates, but instance data does not require transformation.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 CodeableConcept specializes DataType instead of Element
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The baseDefinition metadata changed from `Element` to `DataType`, but the local CodeableConcept instance content model remains unchanged. Per the scope rule, this is not reported as a local CodeableConcept finding.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Generated class hierarchies, reflection code, and validators should be tested against the R6 `DataType` base. The substantive compatibility analysis belongs in the DataType/base-artifact report.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: R6 CodeableConcept now points to `DataType` as its base. Any breaking effect on generated inheritance, inherited `id`/`extension`, and common datatype constraints should be assessed in the DataType/base-artifact report rather than duplicated here.

`CodeableConcept.coding` remains type `Coding`. Changes inside Coding, including R6 conformance warnings such as display-without-code behavior, can surface in CodeableConcept instances but are owned by the Coding report.
